# Starting PAYG instalments
## Automatic entry to PAYG instalments
### Entry thresholds
- instalment income from your latest tax return of $4,000 or more
- tax payable on your latest notice of assessment of $1,000 or more
- estimated (notional) tax of $500 or more.

# When are PAYG instalments due?
## Which lodgment cycle applies to you
- Businesses with instalment income of more than $20 million are required to lodge and pay [monthly PAYG instalments](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/payg-instalments/when-are-payg-instalments-due/monthly-payg-instalments).

# Starting PAYG instalments
## Automatic entry to PAYG instalments
If you lodge a tax return with instalment income above the entry threshold, you may be required to pay PAYG instalments.

### Entry thresholds
- instalment income from your latest tax return of $4,000 or more
- tax payable on your latest notice of assessment of $1,000 or more
- estimated (notional) tax of $500 or more.

web.title: To vary or not to vary? PAYG instalments for the new financial year
web.description:
# To vary or not to vary? PAYG instalments for the new financial year
## Who is required to pay PAYG instalments?
A taxpayer only needs to pay PAYG instalments if they have been notified by the ATO, typically through myGov, Online services for business or by mail.

Taxpayers whose assessable income has only consisted of withholding payments (other than non-quotation withholding payments) are not required to pay PAYG instalments.

The Commissioner is not obliged under legislation to require a taxpayer to make PAYG instalments — the ATO effectively has discretion to determine [entry thresholds](https://www.ato.gov.au/Business/PAYG-instalments/Starting-PAYG-instalments/) for the PAYG instalment system. Taxpayers are automatically required to pay PAYG instalments if:

for an individual (including a sole trader) or trust, they have:

- Business and investment income in their most recent tax return of $4,000 or more
- Tax payable on their latest notice of assessment of $1,000 or more, _and_
- Estimated tax for the current income year of $500 or more.

- Have business and investment income in their most recent tax return of $2 million or more
- Have estimated tax for the current income year of $500 or more, _or_

Taxpayers that are new to business can start voluntary PAYG instalments to help smooth out their cashflow and avoid a large tax bill in their second year of business.

## How many PAYG instalments are payable?
Taxpayers with business and investment income of more than $20 million are required to make monthly PAYG instalments.

# Stopping PAYG instalments
## Automatic exit
### Individuals
- have an estimated (notional) tax liability of less than $500

### Trusts
- has an estimated (notional) tax liability of less than $500
- reports instalment income of less than $4,000 in its tax return
